notes: Approved in round 1: SPW-001/002/003 match the Windows rules and have no blocking defects. Non-blocking notes: desktop_shortcut_manager.sh:553-568 remove still runs the root '$sudo rm -f' on the new filed paths (_dsm_filed_launchers '[ -f ]' follows a user-planted category-dir symlink) -> run it through _dsm_as_user "$u" rm -f -- "$file" like create/edit; :1429 and :1470 treat an account as root by the name 'root', so a second uid-0 account with a Desktop re-enters _dsm_org_run_as_user recursively -> compare the uid; :1324-1334 a manifest reformatted by a JSON tool parses to 0 entries and is still marked UndoneAt -> refuse to close a manifest whose Entries parse to 0 while the file has entries; GNOME (Debian 13 / Ubuntu 26.04 default) may not launch .desktop files inside the category folders from Nautilus -> check this on a real GNOME desktop.

SPW-001 organizer (correctness vs Window.reason:
Every rule below mirrors Get-DesktopOrganizationPlan, Resolve-DesktopPlanCollisions and Get-DesktopPlacementDecision.
- Keyword table: I re-extracted both tables read-only and mapped the GlobalVars DESKTOP_CATEGORY_* names. diff finds 1084 identical category|keyword pairs, in the same order.
- awk matcher (LC_ALL=C): it uses the same token boundaries as $script:DesktopTokenBoundaryPattern. Keywords of 3 chars or fewer must start the text, non-ASCII keywords match as substrings with a code-point score, and the winner is chosen by score, then rank (app list 0 over keywords 1), then category order. Supported categories come from both the Name and Exec-basename matches, with generic hosts blanked.
- Plan: the order is pinned, then broken, then unmatched, then move/copy. Browsers plus a chrome/edge Name token is copied. A filed launcher is refiled only when its category differs and is not supported.
- Collisions: keyed by <Category>/<file>, case-sensitive as Linux requires. The newest wins by strict -nt, identical launchers (cmp -s) follow the winner, and the rest become conflicts.
- _dsm_org_decide: place, unchanged, duplicate, replace (strictly newer) or conflict, with refile onto an existing name always a conflict.
- Preview uses the same decision. A follower of an already-placed destination is labelled unchanged (copy), conflict (refile) or duplicate (move), which is more accurate than the Windows preview. Preview counts a missing folder or link as a change, so 'Nothing to move' means the run writes no manifest.
- Only regular, non-symlink *.desktop files are scanned. window-launcher (the id 193 uses) stays on the Desktop. Broken-Exec launchers stay and are reported. Nothing is deleted: the organizer only uses mv, cp and ln and puts displaced files under state/displaced/<runId>.

SPW-001 idempotency (traced).reason:
Traced the second-run state for each case:
- Moved launchers have left the Desktop, and filed ones are supported in their folder, so there is no refile.
- Copy-mode Chrome/Edge are identical, so unchanged.
- Collision losers and not-newer items are conflicts.
- The folders and links exist.
The result is 0 changes and no manifest.

Installers do not churn:
- _dsm_write_desktop_icon writes into the filed copy when one exists (and into both for a keep-copy browser).
- 154 desktop_icon_exists also scans the filed folders, so it does not recreate Desktop icons.
- desktop_entry_manager.sh's DESKTOP_FALLBACK is unused.

Replace pairs and follower groups converge after one run. The owner's WSL sandbox (preview 2, run 2, run 3: 'Nothing to move'; 1 manifest) matches this trace.

SPW-003 menu, CLI, hint.reason: The menu path is dd.sh > Linux Management > Linux System Tools (linux_management.sh:578/608) > Management & Backup > Organize Desktop Icons [Organize/Preview/Undo]. The back indexes are correct: 2 in the parent menu, 3 in the child menu. The CLI is desktop_shortcut_manager.sh organize|preview|undo [manifest], guarded by BASH_SOURCE==$0 and inert when sourced by the 10 other installers, plus refresh_desktop_icons.sh with the same arguments. 154 runs the organizer last and logs 'Undo: <menu path> > Undo (<manifest>)'. The owner used the library as the CLI instead of a new desktop_icon_organizer.sh, because the task's write scope lists no new file; this is recorded in the ledger and the report and accepted.

root runs act as the user.reason: A root organize, preview or undo of another user's Desktop feeds the library over stdin to 'runuser -u <user> -- env -u CORE_NODE_DESKTOP_ICONS_DIR -u XDG_STATE_HOME -u USE_SUDO -u SUDO_USER ... bash -s'. The nested call ends with </dev/null; under bash -s, BASH_SOURCE is empty, so the direct-run guard stays inert. Undo of an explicit manifest runs as the file's owner (stat without -L). create and edit write user launchers through _dsm_as_user (tee, chmod and sed -i as the user), and gio trust runs as the user. The old symlink-following chown is gone. util-linux (runuser) is Essential on Debian and Ubuntu.

shared helpers / no duplicates.reason: 154's entry_exec_target and inline existence test were replaced by _dsm_entry_exec_target/_dsm_exec_program_exists. The new parser skips env, VAR=value and -options and handles quoted paths, which the old sed/awk parser got wrong. The trust block was extracted to _dsm_trust_launcher. Discovery reuses _dsm_login_users and _dsm_desktop_dir; there is no second path. refresh_desktop_icons.sh uses _dsm_sudo instead of raw sudo, which the DD guide requires ($USE_SUDO). No other Linux organizer or trust implementation exists (grep).

issues: non-blocking: desktop_shortcut_manager.sh:553-568 remove_desktop_shortcut_from_desktop_shortcut_manager still deletes user launchers with the root '$sudo rm -f', now including _dsm_filed_launchers paths. '[ -f ]' follows a user-planted desktopIcons/<Category> symlink, so root can delete <id>.desktop in any directory. The same class already existed through XDG_DESKTOP_DIR in user-dirs.dirs. Fix: run the per-user rm as the user (_dsm_as_user "$u" rm -f -- "$file"), as the owner's own root-acts-as-user rule requires.

non-blocking: desktop_shortcut_manager.sh:1429 and :1470 decide 'root' by account name. A second uid-0 login account (toor-style) with a Desktop dir goes through _dsm_org_run_as_user, and the nested run is still EUID 0. It iterates every login user again and re-enters itself without bound. Fix: test the uid ([ "$(id -u "$user")" -eq 0 ]) and handle uid-0 accounts directly.

non-blocking: desktop_shortcut_manager.sh:1324-1334 and :1388 undo parses only its own one-line entry format. A manifest pretty-printed by a JSON tool parses to 0 entries, reports '0 restored, 0 error(s)' and is marked UndoneAt without restoring anything. Fix: treat 0 parsed entries in a manifest with a non-empty Entries array as an error and keep it open.

non-blocking (verify on hardware): GNOME is the default desktop on Debian 13 and Ubuntu 26.04. Modern Nautilus opens .desktop files inside regular folders as text instead of launching them; only DING on the Desktop launches them. Filed launchers opened through the <Category> link may therefore not start. KDE/XFCE are unaffected. Check this on a real GNOME session, which the owner already lists as remaining.

non-blocking: desktop_shortcut_manager.sh:686 checks '[ -r .../linux_applications_list.sh ]' only because the nested stdin run resolves DSM_LIB_DIR to '/'. Skipping the source when DSM_ORG_APP_SIGNALS is already set would drop the existence check (AGENTS.md: callers trust resolved SH references). Also, :1339-1340 derives the undone store from ${manifest%/*}, which breaks for a bare relative manifest name -> resolve it to an absolute path first.
